cross_case_findings: Metrics use 512 bytes per sector and 1048576 bytes per MiB. Full pressure percentages equal stall microseconds divided by window microseconds times 100. Completion ratio is completion_ms divided by baseline_completion_ms; larger values mean slower completion. Numeric metric values are rounded to six decimals.

Four provider-429 cases complete at 2.125000 times baseline with tiny local pressure. Four memory-pressure cases complete at 2.250000 times baseline with 300 MiB available and bidirectional swapping. Their similar completion delays have different evidence; low send latency in the 429 cases favors delay after sending, while elevated sends in the memory cases support a local contribution. No timing breakdown proves exclusive causality.

Four long-reader cases grow the WAL by 8000 pages with zero checkpoint progress and one active copy. Their 11.111111% to 16.666667% IO full pressure establishes local stalls, while completion is only 1.025000 times baseline. Reader pinning is likely; neither the copy count nor device sectors apportions traffic or proves the copy caused the checkpoint stall.

Four DELETE-journal cases have eight busy errors each and 1.050000 completion ratios, supporting contention with modest observed delay. Eight healthy cases complete at baseline with tiny full pressure and checkpoint progress; four show active checkpoints and four have small WALs. WAL endpoint differences and checkpoint counts alone cannot reconstruct append or reset history.

Physical write rates span 22.583333 to 40.768750 MiB/s; reads are 0.250000 times writes in every case. Logical-to-physical write ratios span 1.000000 to 5.000000 across both healthy and stressed cases. These ratios are not physical write amplification, and cannot establish compression, coalescing, cache effects or device saturation without matched counter scope and timing. Pressure counters, completion spans and device IO lack process attribution and guaranteed alignment; all proposed next checks remain unperformed.
